content_html:
Self-hosted, file-first personal AI assistant built on Pi.

Italiano · Features · Backup · Updates · Decisions

Chat · Second Brain · Projects · Artifacts · Automations · Telegram · Web research

Warning

Memora v0.2.0 is the current public release. The core is usable and tested; restore/update/rollback validation is continuing. Do not expose the service to the public Internet without HTTPS, a reverse proxy and a review of your configuration.

Memora is a self-hosted personal assistant built on Pi. It brings persistent chats, a Markdown-based Second Brain, human-reviewed memory, projects, artifacts, web research and scheduled automations into one interface.

The complete feature registry, with status and known limitations, is in docs/FEATURES.md. Architectural decisions are documented in docs/DECISIONS.md.

Screenshots

A real answer, generated artifact and live preview in the workspace.

Appearance
Theme, density, text size and accessibility.

Status

v0.2.0: features are usable and tested. Installation has been verified on a Debian 13 VM; restore, update and rollback verification is still pending. See docs/FEATURES.md for the current registry and known limitations. Release notes: v0.2.0.

Key features

  • Streaming chat, persistent Pi sessions and background turns.
  • File-first Second Brain: authoritative Markdown and a rebuildable SQLite index.
  • Optional local embeddings with semantic and hybrid retrieval.
  • Memory Inbox with explicit approval by default and optional auto-save; optional LLM Memory Curator.
  • Projects, indexed sources, project files and versioned artifacts.
  • PDF, DOCX, XLSX and PPTX generation without LibreOffice.
  • SSRF-safe web research through Brave or SearXNG, with numbered citations.
  • Scheduled automations with cron/timezone, run history and optional MCP access.
  • Single-user login, browser notifications, optional Telegram delivery and bidirectional Telegram sessions, including private forum groups with one topic per session, per-topic projects and agent profiles with optional project title prefixes, plus an IT/EN/FR interface.
  • One-click update from Administration with a mandatory encrypted backup.
  • Responsive layout, chat side panel and runtime administration.

Requirements

  • Node.js 24
  • pnpm 12.21
  • Debian 13 or a compatible distribution for the full runtime
  • Optional headless Chromium for PDF rendering
  • Optional local embedding model for semantic search

Quick start

git clone https://github.com/lian84/memora.git
cd memora
cp .env.example .env
pnpm install
pnpm dev

Open http://127.0.0.1:3000, complete the first-run setup and configure the provider, model and credentials in Administration.

Production build:

pnpm build
pnpm start

For a Debian systemd installation with backup, restore and update support:

sudo ./install.sh

See Install, restore and update.

Design principles

  1. Pi is the agent engine and remains an external dependency, not a fork.
  2. Important memory remains readable as Markdown.
  3. Sessions remain in Pi JSONL format.
  4. Credentials never enter the repository.
  5. The default deployment is local/LAN; public exposure requires HTTPS and an explicit configuration.
  6. Memora must remain useful when models or frontends change.
  7. Code, configuration, data and secrets are separate; runtime data lives in MEMORA_DATA_DIR.
  8. No user- or machine-specific paths are hardcoded.

Responses can continue in the background: concurrency is configurable in Administration (1–4, default 2) and additional turns are queued. Closing the browser does not stop a turn; restarting Memora does. The sidebar shows a yellow dot for a response running in another chat and a green dot for a completed unread response. Read state is shared across devices, while browser notifications are opt-in and require the tab to stay open. Scheduled automations run in the server and can deliver their results to Telegram with the browser closed. Returning to a chat reconnects to events already produced and resumes partial text. After a server restart, in-flight turns are marked as interrupted.

Stack

  • Debian 13
  • Node.js 24 LTS
  • TypeScript
  • pnpm workspaces
  • @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
  • Fastify
  • React + Vite
  • SQLite + FTS5
  • Markdown as the authoritative source

Quick commands

pnpm install
pnpm dev
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build

The complete list is in Commands.

Contributing

Guidelines, development setup and the Developer Certificate of Origin are in CONTRIBUTING.md. Before a significant change, open an issue to discuss the design.

Security

Do not open public issues for vulnerabilities. Use GitHub private vulnerability reporting; details are in SECURITY.md.

License

Memora is distributed under the terms of AGPL-3.0-only. Contributions are accepted under the same license and require a DCO sign-off. The Memora and Memo names are covered by TRADEMARKS.md; third-party notices are in NOTICE.
